security_audit.summary: Most static Ruby backtick findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and inline file references, not executable Ruby code. The skill still includes risky CI guidance for Kubernetes TLS, Docker login, Terraform apply, and non-blocking security scans. No prompt injection language was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Docker login passes a password on the command line.
remediation.suggestion: Use docker login with --password-stdin and masked protected GitLab variables.
Remove --insecure-skip-tls-verify=true and configure a trusted cluster CA certificate.
Require plan review, protected environments, and approval before applying infrastructure changes.

remediation.issue: Container security scanning is allowed to fail.
remediation.suggestion: Block high and critical findings unless a documented exception is approved.

semantic_findings.title: Docker Password Passed on Command Line
semantic_findings.description: The Docker login example passes CI_REGISTRY_PASSWORD with the -p flag. Command-line password use can expose secrets through process listings or logs if copied directly.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The line directly uses docker login -p with a CI secret. GitLab masking reduces log risk, but password-stdin is the safer documented pattern.

semantic_findings.title: Insecure Kubernetes TLS Verification
semantic_findings.description: The Kubernetes deployment template sets --insecure-skip-tls-verify=true while configuring a token-based cluster connection. This can disable certificate validation for deployments.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The insecure TLS flag is explicit on the kubectl cluster setup command. It appears in a reusable deployment template that users may copy.

semantic_findings.title: Terraform Apply Uses Auto Approve
semantic_findings.description: The Terraform pipeline runs terraform apply -auto-approve against a saved plan. This can apply infrastructure changes without Terraform confirmation if CI gates are weak.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The auto-approve flag is explicit. The job is manual and limited to main, so the risk depends on protected branch and environment controls.

semantic_findings.title: Security Scan Is Allowed to Fail
semantic_findings.description: The Trivy scan is configured to exit on high or critical findings, but allow_failure is true. Vulnerable images could continue through the pipeline.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The scan command targets HIGH and CRITICAL findings, and the same job allows failure. This weakens the security control shown by the example.

content.value_statement: GitLab CI setup can be slow when teams rebuild common patterns from memory. This skill provides reusable pipeline examples for builds, tests, deployments, scanning, caching, and child pipelines.
actual_capabilities: Shows staged GitLab CI patterns for build, test, deploy, Docker, Terraform, scanning, caching, and child pipelines.
Provides YAML examples for artifacts, cache keys, environments, and manual production deployment gates.
Demonstrates Docker image builds and registry pushes with GitLab CI variables.
Outlines Kubernetes deployment jobs for staging and production namespaces.
Includes GitLab security templates and a Trivy container scan example.
limitations: Examples require project-specific validation before production use.
Referenced resource and asset files are not included in this package.
Placeholder domains, application names, and namespaces must be replaced.
Deployment snippets assume existing runners, variables, and Kubernetes access.

use_cases.title: Create a First GitLab Pipeline
use_cases.description: Build a staged pipeline with dependency install, tests, build artifacts, and a controlled deploy path.

use_cases.title: Standardize Container Delivery
use_cases.description: Design Docker build and push jobs that use GitLab registry variables and repeatable image tags.

use_cases.title: Add Pipeline Security Checks
use_cases.description: Add SAST, dependency scanning, container scanning, and review points to an existing CI workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Basic Pipeline
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gitlab-ci-patterns to design a simple GitLab CI pipeline for my project. Include build, test, cache, artifacts, and deploy notes.

prompt_templates.title: Add Docker Delivery
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gitlab-ci-patterns to add Docker image build and registry push jobs. Explain required GitLab variables and safe tag choices.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Multi-Environment Deployments
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gitlab-ci-patterns to create a staging and production deployment plan. Include manual gates, protected environments, and rollback checks.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Complex CI Design
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced audit of an existing pipeline.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gitlab-ci-patterns to review my GitLab CI design for performance, security scanning, Terraform safety, caching, and child pipeline structure.

output_examples.input: Create a Node.js GitLab pipeline with build, test, and deploy stages.
output_examples.output: A staged pipeline outline with dependency caching, build artifacts, test reports, environment settings, and deployment verification steps.

output_examples.input: Add security scanning to an existing container pipeline.
output_examples.output: Recommended GitLab security templates, a container scan step, failure policy guidance, and notes for handling approved exceptions.

output_examples.input: Plan a Terraform workflow in GitLab CI.
output_examples.output: A validate, plan, and apply workflow with artifact handling, approval gates, protected branches, and review requirements.

best_practices: Replace placeholder domains, image names, namespaces, and variables before use.
Review deployment and infrastructure jobs with repository owners before enabling automatic execution.
Use protected variables and environments for registry, Kubernetes, and Terraform credentials.
anti_patterns: Copying deployment snippets into production without validating permissions, gates, and rollback behavior.
Leaving high-severity security scan failures non-blocking without a documented exception policy.
Using latest image tags or broad runner permissions for critical pipelines.

faq.question: Does this skill execute CI commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and YAML examples. GitLab executes commands only after users commit pipeline files.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it include complete template files?
faq.answer: No. Only SKILL.md is present. Referenced asset and reference files are not included.

faq.question: Is it safe to copy the examples directly?
faq.answer: No. Review variables, permissions, environments, and security gates before using any pipeline in production.

faq.question: What project types does it fit best?
faq.answer: It fits GitLab projects that need build, test, Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, or scanning workflows.

faq.question: Does it replace a DevOps review?
faq.answer: No. It helps draft patterns, but production pipelines still need project-specific testing and review.
